newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nuclear waste ship to arrive in Japan on March 18.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear waste ship to arrive in Japan on March 18.

text.p: A British freighter carrying about 20 tonnes of radioactive waste from France will arrive at a port in northern Japan on March 18, an industry group confirmed on Tuesday.

The toxic waste, carried by the Pacific Teal, is due to arrive at Mutsu-Ogawara port on the northern tip of Japan's main island of Honshu, the Federation of Electric Power Companies said in a statement issued jointly with Japan Nuclear Fuel Ltd.
The port is located within the reprocessing plant complex at Rokkasho village in Aomori Prefecture, which is operated by JNFL.
The environmental group Greenpeace said last week that the ship was likely to arrive on March 18.
It is the second shipment of nuclear waste that is being returned to Japan after being processed by French state company COGEMA.
Under the terms of a treaty by Japan, Britain and France, spent Japanese uranium fuel is reprocessed into plutonium at a French plant, and the waste produced must be stored in Japan.
The nuclear waste is mixed in glass and encased in 40 canisters which are then stored in two large containers.
Environmental and protest groups plan to camp out near the complex on March 17 to protest the arrival of the vessel the following day, a Greenpeace spokesman said last week.
